newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes face tight competition in Gulf.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes face tight competition in Gulf.

text.p: U.S. foreign crudes were seen up against stiff competition in the U.S. Gulf due to competing domestic grades and narrow trans-Atlantic opportunities.
Traders said freight rates had eased somewhat but tight profit margins for sellers would prohibit an influx of cargoes for late September and early October.
One million barrels of Norwegian Oseberg was sold into the U.S. Gulf on Wednesday to two refiners at Oct West Texas Intermediate minus five cents cif for early October.
A European seller was also heard offering Brent for the same timing at WTI minus five to 10 cents cif.
Latin American supplies, meanwhile, remained abundant with Mendanitos sold at WTI minus $1.65 fob this week, and Oriente was offered for Oct into the U.S. at WTI minus $1.80 cif.
In the aftermarket, Oct Brent partials moved twice at $22.20 a barrel, slightly above IPE's settlement. Ahead of the trading window, Brent intermonth Oct/Nov traded at 67 cents.
